description:
Dolt is a SQL database that you can fork, clone, branch, merge, push and pull just like a git repository.

Dolt is a SQL database that you can fork, clone, branch, merge, push and pull just like a git repository.
Connect to Dolt just like any MySQL database to run queries or update the data using SQL commands.
Use the command line interface to import CSV files, commit your changes, push them to a remote, or merge your teammate's changes.
Minor Version Bump
This release is a minor version bump due to storage changes made to support merge conflict resolution. When conflicts arise in merging schema changes, the artifacts persisted to disk will be unreadable by older versions of Dolt. Since backwards compatibility is not possible in this case, we've bumped minor version number.
Merged PRs
dolt
- 12334: go: Allow merge to work when the two branches have applied the same primary key change on both sides.
  The merge operation rekeys the altered tables in the common ancestor, so that all three schemas match as required. Conflict readers rekey the same way.
  Changes MergeArtifacts to store the rekeyed base so that it persists across replication, push and GC in the case that the common ancestor was rekeyed in this way.
  Fixes #12012
- 12333: dolt_preview_merge_conflicts: fix swapped base, our and their schemas
  getConflictSchemasFromRoots returned the schemas in the order (ours, theirs, base), but its caller reads them as (base, ours, theirs). When the schemas differed between branches, the preview showed the wrong columns and decoded each side's values with another side's layout.
  Fixes #12330
- 12319: dolt_query_diff: compare matched row values by column type
  - Add diff.ValuesEqual to use column type's Compare, and compare text exactly. Equal out-of-band content addresses skip reading both values.
    Fix #12262
- 12291: sqle: Keep temporary tables across GC.
  sqle: Keep temporary tables across GC.
- 12290: go/libraries/doltcore/sqle/dsess: Write savepoint roots before keeping them in VisitGCRoots
  go/libraries/doltcore/sqle/dsess: Write savepoint roots before keeping them in VisitGCRoots
- 12289: go/store/prolly: roll back flushed edits when a statement with no checkpointed edits fails
  go/store/prolly: roll back flushed edits when a statement with no checkpointed edits fails
- 12279: go: Remove Dolt's dependencies on the global variable registries.
  Part of a body of work to remove the global SystemVariables and StatusVariables registries and make them state on the Engine itself.
  - Dolt no longer falls back to the global registries, and NewSqlEngine and sqlserver.Serve now require a variable bundle.
  - Dolt's system variable definitions are merged into one list.
  - DefaultSession and NewDetachedSession are deprecated.
- 12278: go: Store the commits of a rebase plan as commit addresses.
  New dolt_rebase plans store commit_hash with CommitAddrEnc, so garbage collection keeps the commits of a paused rebase even when no branch reaches them. Writes to the column reject anything but an existing commit before it reaches the store, where a dangling address would discard the shared memtable. Older clients fail reading these plans with a clean error from a new schema field, and plans they wrote keep working as text.
- 12276: go: Keep rebase state and the pre-merge head reachable through working sets.
  WalkAddrs skipped a working set's rebase state and pre-merge head commit, so GC could collect them and leave the database unreadable. WorkingSetHashes now also keeps the pre-merge head for in-memory working sets. Fixes #12253.
- 12240: go/cmd/dolt/commands/sqlserver: Run the read-only access mode check inside a GC safepoint session command.
  With context validation enabled by an earlier engine in the process, as in DoltgreSQL's startup integrity check, loading databases in this check panicked. ConfigureServices now creates one GCSafepointController, shared by this check and the engine through the new SqlEngineConfig.GCSafepointController field.
- 12226: Add dolt branch --orphan to start an unrelated history
  dolt branch --orphan <name> [<start-point>] and dolt_branch('--orphan', ...) create a branch whose only commit has no parents and holds the contents of the start point (HEAD by default). The commit message names the start point, so an orphan of the initial commit never hashes to the same commit. Use dolt commit --amend to change the message.
  Git has the --orphan option in three commands: checkout, switch, and workspace. I decided to deviate for Dolt because checkout is discouraged in a server context, and there is nothing like switch and workspace. Creating a new branch is actually a better description of what is happening anyway.
  Additionally: checkout permission bug addressed.
  Related: #4468
